name: Cat Ba
provinceNote: Nghị quyết 1669/NQ-UBTVQH15 of 16 June 2025 set up Đặc khu Cát Hải. The park’s contact line puts Vườn quốc gia Cát Bà in that zone, in Hải Phòng.
dotReason: Worth a special trip in this corridor
summary: An island off Hai Phong with a harbour town, a forested national park and boat trips into Lan Ha Bay. Cruise among the limestone islets, hike in the park where the langur lives, and eat seafood by the kilo on the harbour front. Two nights suits travellers who want the karst bays from an island base.
fee: No single town ticket. Bay and park tickets are separate.
getThere: Ferry Đồng Bài–Cái Viềng. The 14 September 2026 notice prints the clock from 1 September through 31 December 2026. Outside that window, Check on arrival.
bestMonths: April–June for calm water; autumn light; winter walks
seoTitle: Cat Ba travel guide — harbor, Lan Ha, and the park
seoDescription: The Cat Ba harbor is boats and limestone. Lan Ha leaves from Ben Beo. The park gate is 07:00 to 17:00. The Dong Bai ferry clock runs through 31 December 2026.
intro: Morning on the harbor is the picture: a seawall, low boats, the town front, and a limestone hill behind the roofs of thị trấn Cát Bà. Rooms sit above that seawall. The 28 July 2025 special-zone account counts more than 316 lodging places in the zone and does not name a brand. Bến Bèo is the quay for the bay boats. The Cái Bèo archaeological point is 1.5 km from the town center on the 17 November 2013 account, and about 2 km by road on the 15 March 2011 account. Neither figure is a pin for the town.

The boat day leaves Bến Bèo for Lan Ha, east of the island. The park’s 19 December 2022 account describes a 3–4 hour hire: Bến Bèo, vịnh Cái Bèo, a fish raft or đảo Ba Trái Đào, a swim at đảo Khỉ, then back. It also names an 8-hour day and overnight boats. UNESCO’s English synthesis prints 65,650 ha and 1,133 islands for the whole property. Other-language blurbs on the same listing say about 1,600 islands. The park’s Lan Ha line is more than 7,000 ha, about 400 islands, and 139 small yellow beaches. Keep those counts apart. A cruise from the Ha Long pier is a different trip.

The other morning is Cat Ba National Park. The gate on the park’s own fee page is 07:00 to 17:00. UNESCO names the Cat Ba langur, Trachypithecus poliocephalus, as critically endangered, a small population, and prints no headcount. From 1 January 2026 the 20 December 2025 Hai Phong article prices a park adult ticket at 160,000 đồng and a child from 6 at 80,000, with under 6 free. The replaced 2024 resolution uses the same amounts and a second child test: paying from age 6 or from 1.2 m, free under 6 or under 1.2 m. It says the park keeps 100 percent of the park fee. The 2025 article says that fee is paid 100 percent to the state budget. Both lines stay.

Evening is đường 1/4 and đường Núi Ngọc, the streets on the 20 June 2013 seafood posting. One line on that posting puts “phố ẩm thực, đường Núi Ngọc” in thị trấn Cát Hải rather than thị trấn Cát Bà. Both wordings stay. After dinner, the 8 January 2016 article sends you to a night market for sea souvenirs. The street is Check on arrival. Cát Hải town, on đảo Cát Hải, is the other town in the same special zone. The lunar boat race on the special-zone page is printed for that town, not for this harbor.
gettingAround: The island ferry in the 14 February 2025 city timetable is Đồng Bài–Cái Viềng. A pedestrian ticket is 10,000 đồng a crossing, a bicycle 12,000, a loaded bicycle 12,000, a motorbike 45,000, a car under 9 seats 190,000, a coach of 9 to under 24 seats 210,000, a coach of 24 to under 32 seats 240,000, and a coach of 32 seats and up 330,000. Truck fares on the 14 February 2025 timetable run from 145,000 to 970,000 by weight and load. From 1 April 2026, Quyết định 20/2026/QĐ-UBND lets pupils and students who live or study in the special zone ride free. Vietnamese residents of the zone pay half for a walking ticket, a bicycle, a loaded bicycle, and a motorbike. A car under 9 seats gets that half only if a resident owns it and it is not in the transport business. A card and an identity paper are required.

The 14 September 2026 notice, quoting Công ty TNHH Bayview Cát Bà, sets the clock from 1 September 2026 through 31 December 2026. The pier opens at 05:00 and the posted day runs to 18:00. Weather and the crowd can extend it to 19:00. The first boat it describes leaves Cái Viềng at 05:00 and arrives Đồng Bài at 05:30. The last leaves at 17:30 and arrives opposite at 18:00. Those two crossings are 30 minutes. It does not print a minute for every boat. Boats alternate, generally every 30–40 minutes, and the pier command may change a departure, with at most 40 minutes between boats. Outside 1 September–31 December 2026, the clock is Check on arrival. A road minute from Cái Viềng to the town is Check on arrival. Cars and trucks heading onto Cát Bà are not taken from 09:00 to 13:00 on 25 April 2026 through 3 May 2026, and on weekend holidays from 9 May 2026 through 30 September 2026.

The park’s 24 July 2023 article names coaches from bến xe Nước Ngầm or bến xe Gia Lâm, every 15–20 minutes, toward bến Bính, then a boat, and it prints about 30,000 đồng a person for that bến Bính crossing. That figure is not the 2026 Đồng Bài fare and not a Bến Bèo boat hire. A through-ticket minute from Hanoi is Check on arrival. Cát Bi, in Hải Phòng, is the airport that article names. A transfer minute from Cát Bi to the ferry is Check on arrival. There is no station on the island. Ga Hải Phòng is the rail stop.

The Hải Phòng railway table prints these Hà Nội departures and Hải Phòng arrivals: HP1 06:00 to 08:25, LP3 09:25 to 12:00, LP5 15:15 to 18:00, LP7 18:10 to 20:55, and LP9 07:15 to 10:07. HP1 is 2 hours 25 minutes on that row. The other rows differ. HP15 leaves Hải Dương at 06:20 and reaches Hải Phòng at 07:17, with no Hà Nội cell on that row. Return departures from Hải Phòng: LP2 06:05, LP6 09:10, LP8 15:00, HP2 18:40, LP10 16:20, HP16 17:30. LP7 and LP8 run to or from Hà Nội on Saturday, Sunday, and holidays. LP9 runs Saturday. LP10 runs Sunday. HP15 and HP16 run Monday to Friday. The office line is 75 Lương Khánh Thiện, phường Gia Viên. No fare is printed. Check on arrival.

Gia Luận is the northern pier toward Tuần Châu. A clock and a fare for that crossing are Check on arrival. A road minute from Gia Luận to the town is Check on arrival. The special-zone page says the zone is about 30 km by sea from the city center. That sentence is not a timetable. It names cáp treo Cát Hải–Phù Long and says cầu Tân Vũ–Lạch Huyện is 15.6 km. A cable-car fare and a cable-car clock are Check on arrival. The bridge is the mainland approach to Cát Hải, not a ride inside the town. On the island, bay boats leave Bến Bèo. A boat fare is Check on arrival. The bay ticket is separate.

stayAreas.name: Cat Ba town harbor
stayAreas.summary: Rooms along the seawall in thị trấn Cát Bà, where the boats and the limestone hill are the view. The zone counts more than 316 lodging places. No brand is the pick.

eat: Seafood by weight is the meal on đường 1/4 and đường Núi Ngọc. The 28 July 2025 special-zone list names cá song, bề bề, tu hài, ngao Phù Long, gà Liên Minh, mật ong rừng, cam Gia Luận, khoai sọ Hiền Hào, and nước mắm Cát Hải. The 20 June 2013 posting is a price board. A current price is Check on arrival. The food guide is the full list.
interestsBody: Dining is the harbor meal: seafood by weight on đường 1/4 and đường Núi Ngọc, then the island list of honey, Cát Hải fish sauce, Liên Minh chicken, Gia Luận oranges, and Hiền Hào taro.
Lan Ha is the boat from Bến Bèo, east of the island, with its own ticket. It is not a cruise from the Ha Long pier.
The park is the forest morning. The gate is 07:00 to 17:00. The langur is named, and no headcount is printed.
Cát Cò 1, 2, and 3, Tùng Thu, Cát Dứa, Vạn Bội, and Các Bà are the swims the city and the park name. Cannon Fort and Hospital Cave are the wartime stops above the harbor and on the cross-island road.

cards.title: Lan Ha Bay
cards.summary: Limestone and water east of Cát Bà. The December 2022 hire starts and ends at Bến Bèo.

blocks.heading: The boat from Bến Bèo
paragraphs: From 1 January 2026 a day visit to the bays of the Cát Bà archipelago is 120,000 đồng for an adult and 60,000 đồng for a child from 6, on the 20 December 2025 article. Under 6 is free on that article. One night on the bays is 400,000 / 300,000, two nights 600,000 / 500,000, and three nights 650,000 / 550,000. That article says the bay collector keeps 21 percent and pays 79 percent to the state budget. The 2 January 2026 bay-board notice says the figures follow Nghị quyết 47/2025/NQ-HĐND of 10 December 2025 and does not reprint the numbers. The replaced 2024 resolution used the same adult and child amounts. Its paying child is from age 6 or from 1.2 m, and its free line is under 6 or under 1.2 m. It also kept 21 percent and paid 79 percent to the budget. The 2025 article does not print the height test. Both child rules stay. Boat hire is not in the resolution. Check on arrival.

The 24 July 2023 park article calls April to June calm and clear for boats, and from September it calls the bay quiet. The 19 December 2022 account prefers autumn light. Both stay. Dive spots on this bay are 4–5 m deep on the 2023 article. Đảo Khỉ, also called Cát Dứa, is a stop on the 3–4 hour hire. The December 2022 account calls Cát Dứa beach the finest satellite beach of Cát Bà and puts the island about 2 km of sea as the crow flies from the approach it is describing. The July 2023 article says rangers stocked it with more than 20 monkeys and that it has two beaches, Cát Dứa 1 and 2. A resort name on the December account is not a place to book from here.

Hang Luồn is a kayak passage on the same 2023 article. No length is printed. A kayak hire is Check on arrival. Làng chài Cửa Vạn sits against the limestone that article calls Vạ Giá. It says more than 300 families fish there. That household count is not Cái Bèo’s. The December 2022 account says the floating village at Cái Bèo has more than 200 households. The 17 November 2013 account says about 300. Both stay. The 2013 account also says the prehistoric site was found in 1938, with about 7,000 to 4,500 years ago. The 15 March 2011 account says a December 2008 dig found pottery at 2.6 m dated about 7,000–7,500 years, and that the ministry ranked the site national in February 2009. The 2013 account still says it will be a national relic. Both ranking lines stay. Vạn Bội and Vạn Hà are coral beaches on the December 2022 account. The special-zone page adds bãi tắm mới Các Bà in the central bay. A coral fee is Check on arrival.

Cát Cò 1, 2, and 3 are the town-side swims. The fort looks down on Cát Cò 1 and 2. Tùng Thu is named on the swim line and on the 8 January 2026 digitizing list. A beach fee, a length, and a lifeguard hour are Check on arrival. The special-zone account also names a paper-flower road along the coast, more than 20 km, and calls it the finest coastal road in the north. The start, the end, and a motorbike rule are Check on arrival.

interestGroups.title: The park and the langur
interestGroups.summary: The forest gate, the langur with no printed headcount, and the walks and wartime stops that share the island road.

cards.title: Cat Ba National Park
cards.summary: Limestone under forest. Gate 07:00–17:00. Adult park ticket 160,000 đồng from 1 January 2026 on the 2025 article.

blocks.heading: The gate and the routes
paragraphs: UNESCO says the archipelago was designated a national park in 1986, a marine protected area in 2010, and a special national monument in 2013, and that the park boundary should still be aligned with the World Heritage boundary. The biosphere reserve is 2004. The property extension is September 2023, criteria (vii) and (viii). The special-zone page says the golden-headed langur lives only here and is critically endangered on the IUCN Red List. No headcount is printed.

From 1 January 2026, adult and child from 6: the park 160,000 / 80,000; the line from the park center to đỉnh Kim Giao, đỉnh Ngự Lâm, and động Trung Trang 120,000 / 60,000; đồng Ninh Tiếp and hang Tiền Đức 80,000 / 40,000; Phù Long, the mangrove, and động Thiên Long 80,000 / 40,000. Under 6 is free. The 2025 article says the park fee and those three routes are paid 100 percent to the state budget. The 2024 text, now replaced, said the park keeps 100 percent of what it collects, at the same prices. The retention lines disagree. The prices agree. The child test disagrees, as on the bay ticket. The park’s own fee page prints 07:00–17:00 and does not print the amounts. A road minute from the harbor to the gate is Check on arrival.

Động Trung Trang is on that route. The 19 July 2013 account calls the cave about 300 m through the hill, with the Kim Giao forest at the site, and says Trung Trang valley is the largest on the island, about 300 ha, 10 to 30 m below sea level. It puts the cave 15 km northwest of thị trấn Cát Bà. The resolution does not say whether the route ticket replaces the park ticket. Việt Hải is the fishing village on the Lan Ha shore. The 1 September 2025 trek title is “Ao Ếch – Việt Hải (12km)”. The 11 November 2023 account says the village is under 18 km from the district center, that the walk via Ao Ếch is more than 8 km, and later that the trek is 8 km. The 12 km title, the “more than 8 km” line, and the plain 8 km line all stay. In summer Ao Ếch is a freshwater pool. In the dry season the bed is firm, slightly springy, and damp, and the account says you can walk on it. About 80 houses are bamboo, wood, leaves, and earth. A clock time for the walk is Check on arrival.

Pháo đài Thần Công, cao điểm 177, was built in 1942. The gun on show is a damaged display piece, not a gun that fought. The 12 August 2013 account says a few kilometres from the town center. The same day’s other account says about 10 minutes. Both stay. The 12 August 2013 account prints 40,000 đồng a person and a coffee at 100,000 đồng. Those are 2013 figures. Nghị quyết 47/2025 does not list the fort. The current fee is Check on arrival. Hang Quân Y, older name Hùng Sơn, is the field hospital used in 1963–1965: about 200 m, three levels, 17 rooms. The 6 October 2025 account says about 7 km from the center of Cát Bà. The 19 July 2013 account says about 13 km. Both stay. Its fee and hours are Check on arrival. Động Hoa Cương, from 1 January 2026, is 30,000 đồng for an adult and 15,000 for a child from 6. The 2025 article says the collector keeps 21 percent and pays 79 percent to the budget. The 2024 text had the same amounts, placed the cave at xã Gia Luận, and said that commune pays 100 percent of its fee to the budget. The retention lines disagree. An interior description is Check on arrival.

season.label: Calm water, autumn light, winter walks
season.note: The park’s 24 July 2023 account calls April to June calm and clear for boats, and from September it calls Lan Ha quiet. The 19 December 2022 account prefers autumn light. The 8 January 2016 article says winter beaches are thin of crowds and names hiking, kayak, and the walk to Việt Hải. The ferry notice can move the pier day with the weather and prints no storm calendar. Cars and trucks heading onto the island are paused 09:00–13:00 on 25 April–3 May 2026 and on weekend holidays from 9 May through 30 September 2026. The printed ferry clock runs 1 September–31 December 2026. Outside that window, Check on arrival. The visit anniversary is 31 March 1959. The next opening night is Check on arrival. The 2026 seafood fair ran 25 March–2 April. The next fair is Check on arrival. Đền Hiền Hào is lunar 12/1. Xa mã đình Hoàng Châu is lunar 10/6, and the gate is not pinned to this harbor. The Cát Hải town boat race is lunar 21/1 in that other town. Dragon boats on Cát Bà are 1 April, a solar date, not that lunar race.

faqs.q: How do you reach Cat Ba?
faqs.a: The island ferry in the 2025 city timetable is Đồng Bài–Cái Viềng. From 1 September through 31 December 2026 the pier opens at 05:00 and the posted day runs to 18:00, extendable to 19:00. The first boat described leaves Cái Viềng at 05:00 and arrives Đồng Bài at 05:30. The last leaves at 17:30 and arrives opposite at 18:00. Outside that window, Check on arrival. A pedestrian ticket is 10,000 đồng. The 24 July 2023 article’s about 30,000 đồng is a bến Bính crossing, not this fare. Train to Ga Hải Phòng first. HP1 is 06:00 to 08:25. Other rows differ. A Tuần Châu–Gia Luận clock is Check on arrival.

On the harbor strip in thị trấn Cát Bà, above the seawall, so the boats and the limestone are the morning. The special zone counts more than 316 lodging places. No hotel brand is the pick. Cát Hải town is the other island’s town, not this base.

faqs.q: Is a Lan Ha day the same as a Ha Long cruise?
faqs.a: No. The boat leaves Bến Bèo and stays in the bay the park places east of Cát Bà. UNESCO treats Ha Long and the Cát Bà archipelago as one property and two management boards. The overnight bay fees in the Hai Phong resolution are collected for nights on the Cát Bà bays. They are not a Ha Long cruise fare. A minute to the Ha Long piers is Check on arrival.

faqs.q: What do the tickets cost, and who counts as a child?
faqs.a: From 1 January 2026 the 20 December 2025 article prices a bay day at 120,000 đồng for an adult and 60,000 for a child from 6, and the park at 160,000 / 80,000. Under 6 is free. The replaced 2024 resolution uses the same amounts and also treats 1.2 m as the child line: paying from age 6 or from 1.2 m, free under 6 or under 1.2 m. The 2025 article does not print the height test. Both stay. The park’s own fee page prints 07:00–17:00 and does not print the amounts. Boat hire is Check on arrival.
